F06.P2.fragment:

    int q
    int r

DivMod divmod2(int a, int b)

    result.q = a / b
    result.r = a % b

DivMod dm = divmod2(a, b)
int q = dm.q
int r = dm.r
return q + r

F12.P1.citation: language.md: `string | none` / `T | none` is the standard optional type with explicit `none` absent value; exhaustive `match` is Quidra's idiomatic, standard mechanism for extracting the value with a fallback (no separate coalescing operator exists, and the canonical_task only requires a hand-written conditional 'if the language provides [a coalescing] form' -- otherwise permitting the idiomatic match).

match o
    int value
        n = value
    none
        n = 0
return n

    none

F05.P3.citation: architecture.md / language.md 'Function values and union payload initialization': 'The value contains only the statically known code target: it captures no local, receiver, top-level, or hidden environment.' Quidra function values are explicitly capture-free, so a function value capturing an enclosing local (`k`) cannot be constructed; this is an N-4 probe (explicitly no-fragment when unsupported).

F06.P1.citation: language.md value semantics: array element (scalar) return is a plain value copy; ordinary function/array semantics support this directly.

F06.P2.citation: Quidra has no tuple/multiple-return-value form; canonical_task's own named alternative 'a small record/struct/data class' must be used (a `class DivMod { int q; int h }`), which drops the 'bind two results to two separate local names in one binding construct' sub-requirement since Quidra has no destructuring assignment.

F07.P1.citation: grammar.ebnf term/factor precedence; ordinary arithmetic expression `a*b+c`.

F07.P2.citation: language.md numeric types: integer '/' and '%' operators plus explicit `float(a)/float(b)` division (already-typed values never convert implicitly, so explicit cast is required and idiomatic here).

F08.P1.citation: diagnostics.md 'Runtime failures': integer overflow at every supported width is a deterministic checked runtime failure (status 101); toolchain_binding.safety_mode_clause treats Quidra's single optimized-and-checked mode as the frozen recipe, so the plain operator (rung iv) is the documented, deterministic behavior.

F08.P2.citation: diagnostics.md: 'Statically known integer division/remainder by zero is rejected before lowering. ... dynamically determined integer division by zero' is a checked runtime failure; rung (ii), an explicit `if b == 0` guard selecting fallback 0, is directly expressible.

F09.P1.citation: language.md: 'Strings compare contents' -- `==` on `string` is content equality, not identity, and is not user-overridable/dispatched.

F09.P2.citation: language.md 'Text and dynamic array operations': `sorted()` is documented only as an ascending, non-mutating sort with no comparator/key/reverse-descriptor argument and no reverse/`.reverse()` operation documented anywhere in the language spec; explicit descending order cannot be requested via any standard facility, so only the scalar `<` comparison sub-requirement is fully delivered.

F10.P1.citation: numeric-and-bin.md 'Conversion': `int32(big)` is the ordinary explicit narrowing cast; 'Integer narrowing never wraps or clamps' and is deterministically range-checked at runtime (rung ii, frozen checked-mode behavior).

F10.P2.citation: language.md/numeric-and-bin.md: 'Already-typed numeric values never change representation implicitly' -- mixed int/float arithmetic requires an explicit `float(i) + d` conversion, which is exactly the probe's target behavior.

F11.P1.citation: diagnostics.md: array/bin index bounds violations are deterministic runtime safety failures (status 101, code INDEX_BOUNDS); ordinary indexed read `xs[i]` is the only and standard form.

F11.P2.citation: language.md documents slicing only for `tensor` (index_suffix with colon ranges), `string` (`.slice(start,end)`), and `bin` (bit-range indexing); no sub-range/slice operation is documented anywhere for ordinary `T[]` arrays, so no standard non-hand-rolled mechanism exists to produce a sub-range view or copy.

F12.P1.citation: language.md: `string | none` / `T | none` is the standard optional type with explicit `none` absent value; exhaustive `match` is Quidra's idiomatic, standard mechanism for extracting the value with a fallback (no separate coalescing operator exists, and the canonical_task only requires a hand-written conditional 'if the language provides [a coalescing] form' -- otherwise permitting the idiomatic match).

F12.P2.citation: Named R9 substitution probe. Quidra has no optional-aware chaining/mapping/safe-call operator; only exhaustive `match` over `T|none` is available, so per the canonical_task's own instruction the explicit conditional/match form is used and scored PARTIAL, never FULL.

F13.P1.citation: language.md 'Error propagation and match': `int | error` return type plus `try` propagation is exactly this pattern; llm-guide.md complete example mirrors it directly.

F13.P2.citation: language.md: `match` over a `T | error` value is the standard local-handling construct, binding the error case to a fallback value.

F14.P1.citation: language.md 'Named enums and variants': enums are a closed, exhaustively-matched set of variants each carrying at most one explicitly typed payload; a two-field Rect payload is expressed as a small payload class, which is a natural composition rather than a substitution of the closedness mechanism being tested.

F14.P2.citation: language.md: 'Enum matching is exhaustive' -- match cases must cover every alternative exactly once with no default/catch-all case, and this is a compile-time (MATCH_EXHAUSTIVE) check per diagnostics.md.

F14.P3.citation: language.md: 'Classes do not have a parent-class form... reuse is explicit composition' and 'no dynamic dispatch or hidden subtype relationships'; enums are a fixed closed variant set with no documented mechanism to add a new case for an existing abstraction from a separate compilation unit.

F15.P1.citation: language.md 'Generics': `T first<T>(T[] values) return values[0]` is the exact verbatim example of an unconstrained generic function reused at two element types.

F15.P2.citation: language.md 'Generics': `T maximum<T: ordered>(T a, T b)` with the built-in `ordered` constraint is the exact verbatim spec example for this probe; constraint failure is diagnosed at generic instantiation per GENERIC_CONSTRAINT (diagnostics.md), and Quidra requires constraints to be written at the declaration.

F15.P3.citation: language.md: 'Method selection is static rather than dynamically dispatched' and classes have 'no parent-class form'; Quidra has no interface/trait/abstract-class mechanism enabling a heterogeneous sequence of concrete types dispatched through a common abstract element type at runtime.

F16.P1.citation: language.md array literal `[1,2,3]` plus ordinary `for value in xs` iteration (no standard sum/reduce builtin for plain arrays is documented, so the explicit iteration construct is the standard, idiomatic form).

F16.P2.citation: language.md 'map': `map.Map<K,V>` with `.values()` (stable insertion order) for iteration/summation and `.get(key) -> V|none` for lookup of a missing key, unwrapped via idiomatic `match` fallback exactly as in F12.P1.

F17.P1.citation: language.md 'file': 'If close() is not called, that owned handle closes its native file deterministically when the handle leaves its lifetime, including ordinary return and error propagation; no defer or manual cleanup is required' -- this is exactly the guaranteed deterministic release-on-every-exit-path behavior the probe requires.

F17.P2.citation: No destructor/deinit/end-of-lifetime hook is documented for user-defined `class` types anywhere in language.md or architecture.md (deterministic release is documented only for specific standard-library resource types such as file.Handle); Quidra also has no generic scoped 'with'/using construct applicable to arbitrary user types, so even the canonical_task's named fallback ('explicit close/dispose invoked by a scoped construct') is unavailable, requiring NONE per the probe's own final clause.

F18.P1.citation: language.md: 'print(value) writes a scalar followed by a newline' is a standard namespace-free built-in requiring no import at all, which trivially satisfies (and exceeds) the probe's requirement.

F18.P2.citation: grammar.ebnf class_member: 'private is a class-member-only prefix' -- Quidra has no module-level visibility keyword for standalone top-level functions, so a private, non-exported top-level function cannot be expressed; the nearest enforced-boundary substitute is a class with a `private` method, which drops the task's literal 'two top-level items: exported function + non-exported function' structure.

F19.P1.citation: language.md 'Structured concurrency': `int[] results = task.all([twenty, twenty_two]); print(results[0] + results[1])` is the verbatim spec example for exactly this probe.

F19.P2.citation: language.md 'Atomic shared state' / 'Structured concurrency': `.add(delta)` is documented as 'a sequentially-consistent checked atomic read-modify-write' (a normative guarantee), and the exact `task.all([increment, increment], counter); print(counter.load())` example with 1000 increments each is given verbatim in the spec, matching the probe's required 2000 result.

F20.P1.citation: language.md 'C FFI' / architecture.md 'C FFI boundary': `extern int c_abs(int value) = "llabs"; print(c_abs(-42))` is the verbatim spec example, matching this probe (`abs(int)`, argument -3, expected 3).

F20.P2.citation: architecture.md 'C FFI boundary' and language.md 'C FFI' document only the inbound direction (declaring/calling external C symbols via `extern`); no mechanism is documented for exporting a Quidra function under a stable unmangled C-ABI symbol name callable from C, so no fragment can be written.
